item.message: Skill descriptions were shortened to fit the 2% skills context budget. Codex can still see every skill, but some descriptions are shorter. Disable unused skills or plugins to leave more room for the rest.

item.text: {"brief_complete":false,"completion_reason":"Three material validation-risk decisions remain unresolved: whether failed required validation can be overridden, how promotion handles source drift, and what proof cloud providers need before production enablement.","questions":[{"decision_key":"required_validation_override_policy","label":"Failed validation authority","context":"A required validator is an automatic check that must pass before a workflow result reaches manual approval. The provisional direction says manual review follows full automatic validation, but it does not say whether an—","evidence":"`adapters/runtime-adapters/src/harness-executors.mjs` lets harnesses validate and recommend, while `packages/contracts/index.mjs` defines canonical run states. The verified boundary says NexusCentral policy—not model or harness output—must enforce approval gates.","impact":"This determines whether a human can legitimize evidence that failed its declared checks. It shapes every approval gate, the meaning of “validated,” and whether long-term audit records remain mechanically trustworthy.","question":"When a required automatic validator fails, may a human approval override that failure?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"No override; require a new attempt","consequence":"The failed attempt remains failed, and approval becomes available only after a corrected attempt passes. This costs rerun time but preserves a durable rule that approved results always passed their declared validation."},{"number":2,"text":"Allow a recorded exception","consequence":"An authorized operator may accept the failed result with a reason and explicit exception evidence. This handles emergencies quickly but makes downstream consumers distinguish normally validated results from exception-approved ones forever."},{"number":3,"text":"Gate override by workflow policy","consequence":"Each workflow declares whether failed validation is overridable. This provides flexibility but increases authoring, UI, API, and audit complexity and can produce inconsistent safety across workflows."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"A failed validator should remain authoritative evidence rather than become advisory. Requiring a corrected attempt keeps approval semantics simple and prevents gradual erosion of safety across purpose-specific gates.","priority":96},{"decision_key":"simspace_source_drift_promotion_policy","label":"Promotion after source drift","context":"Source drift means the original Coding workspace changes after NexusCentral creates its isolated SimSpace copy but before validated changes are promoted back. Promotion is the separate action that applies validated Sim—","evidence":"`docs/13-HARNESS-EXPERIMENTS.md` requires Codex work in a content-hashed SimSpace copy, followed by validation, approval, and a separate promotion command protecting the source workspace.","impact":"This decides whether validation remains tied to the exact source bytes it assessed. It directly affects lost-work risk, unsafe merges, operator recovery effort, and the long-term integrity of Coding promotions.","question":"What should promotion do when the source workspace no longer matches the hash used to create the validated SimSpace?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"Block and rerun from fresh source","consequence":"Promotion stops and requires a new SimSpace attempt against current source. This adds latency but gives the clearest guarantee that validation covers the exact code being promoted."},{"number":2,"text":"Reapply then fully revalidate","consequence":"NexusCentral attempts to apply the validated change to current source and runs the complete validation suite again before a new approval. This preserves more work but requires robust conflict handling and creates a second evidence lineage."},{"number":3,"text":"Permit explicit forced promotion","consequence":"An operator may bypass the hash mismatch after a warning. This is fast in emergencies but can overwrite concurrent work or promote a combination that was never validated."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"The content hash is the safety link between evidence and promotion. Blocking on drift is the smallest fail-closed contract and avoids making merge correctness part of the initial production trust boundary.","priority":94},{"decision_key":"cloud_provider_live_qualification_policy","label":"Cloud provider qualification","context":"Live qualification means exercising a provider with real credentials and verifying authentication, streaming, cancellation, errors, and routing behavior—not only checking that its request and response formats match a—","evidence":"`packages/contracts/index.mjs` includes OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Google, Azure, and AWS Bedrock presets, but `docs/12-IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md` records only contract-level cloud proof; real cloud credentials remain unproven.","impact":"This sets the production acceptance boundary for Models and Router. It controls whether users can select adapters whose real failure behavior is unknown and establishes the long-term standard for adding provider families safely.","question":"What qualification must a cloud provider family pass before NexusCentral enables it for production routing?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"Live qualification before enablement","consequence":"Each provider family stays disabled until a credentialed acceptance suite proves its critical operations. Launch scope may be narrower, but enabled providers carry a clear, repeatable reliability claim."},{"number":2,"text":"Experimental opt-in after contract proof","consequence":"Operators may explicitly enable unqualified providers with persistent warnings and separated evidence. This expands early coverage but adds degraded-mode UX and transfers operational risk to users."},{"number":3,"text":"Contract proof is sufficient","consequence":"All implemented presets can be enabled at launch. This maximizes availability but may expose authentication, streaming, cancellation, or error-routing failures only in production."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"Provider failures feed directly into queue failover and canonical run evidence. Live qualification keeps the advertised production surface aligned with behavior NexusCentral has actually exercised.","priority":89}]}
